instruction: Add my unpacked Chrome extension from the Desktop to Chrome so I can use it.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

metadata.explanation: Variation 0: Paraphrased instruction to 'load this unpacked extension' instead of 'install'. Task remains identical - loading the helloExtension from Desktop folder. Evaluator checks the extension path is registered in Chrome Preferences. No custom functions needed as we reuse existing get_find_unpacked_extension_path and is_in_list.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator logic correctly verifies the instruction requirement to load an unpacked Chrome extension
Getter (get_find_unpacked_extension_path) extracts the correct state: all installed extension paths from Chrome Preferences file
Metric (is_in_list) performs the correct comparison: checks if the expected extension path is present in the list of registered extensions
Expected value ('/home/user/Desktop/helloExtension') matches the actual extension location from the setup config
Complete coverage: instruction only requires loading the extension, and evaluator checks exactly that by verifying the path is registered in Chrome's internal state
Practical feasibility confirmed: Chrome stores unpacked extension paths in the Preferences file, making this verification approach reliable
